The [ada](#ada){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="annual day aggregate"} is like a [sōzu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shishi-odoshi#:~:text=a%20type%20of%20water%20fountain%20used%20in%20Japanese%20gardens), a Japanese garden fountain that fills until it reaches a tipping point, empties out, and then begins to fill up again. In this analogy,  time flows like water from the [ada](#ada){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="annual day aggregate"} to the [yoe](#yoe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"}, the [eoy](#eoy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="end of year"} is the total volume of the sōzu, the [pia](#pia){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive interval ada"} is the volume that is filled with water, and the absolute value of the [nia](#nia){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative interval ada"} is the volume that is empty: [eoy](#eoy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="end of year"} = [pia](#pia){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive interval ada"} &minus; [nia](#nia){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative interval ada"}. 

::: {.column-margin fig-align="center" .gif #sozu}
![](/asset/Higashiyama_Botanical_Garden_Shishiodoshi_20170617.gif){fig-alt="A bamboo sōzu at Higashiyama Botanical Garden slowly fills with water, tips forward to empty it, and swings back up to fill again"}
[[Wikimedia](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Higashiyama_Botanical_Garden_Shishiodoshi_20170617.gif)]{.giflabel #sozulabel}
:::

# Time of milliday (tom) {#sec-tom .hiddenheading}

Just as we can divide an [ada](#ada){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="annual day aggregates"} into a [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of year"} and [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="times of day"}, we can split a [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} into a "milliday of day" ([mod](#mod){#millidayofday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday of day"}) and a "time of milliday" ([tom](#tom){#timeofmilliday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of milliday"}): [tod](#tod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of day"} = [mod](#mod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday of day"} &times; 100 + [tom](#tom){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of milliday"}. Multiplying a [mod](#mod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday of day"} by 100 converts it from [md](#md){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday"} to [cmd](#cmd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="centimillidays"}. To distinguish the [tom](#tom){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of milliday"} from the [mod](#mod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday of day"}, we can express the first digit of the [tom](#tom){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time of milliday"} in [b9](#b9){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base9"} rather than [b10](#b10){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="base10"}: \${zeroTmonHsl()}\${zeroTtopHsl()} = \${zeroTmonHsl()} &times; 100 + \${zeroTtonHsl()} &asymp; \${zeroTmonHsl()}\${decsepHsl()} = \${zeroTmonHsl()} &times; 100 + \${decsecHsl()}.

# Simulated watch face {#sec-swf .hiddenheading}

The range input below sets the [tzo](#tzo){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="time zone offsets"} for the watch [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clock_face#:~:text=displays%20time%20through%20the%20use%20of%20a%20flat%20dial%20with%20reference%20marks) simulation beneath it. The radio inputs in between the range input and simulation determine whether the simulated watch face is circular or rectangular and whether it has 90 [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"} or 100 [cmd](#cmd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="centimillidays"} [marks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hatch_mark#Unit_and_value_marks:~:text=The%20distance%20between%20adjacent%20marks%20is%20one%20unit). An [md](#md){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday"} divides evenly into thirds, sixths, or ninths with [s](#s){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Dec seconds"}, quarters with [cmd](#cmd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="centimillidays"}, and halves, fifths, or tenths with either unit.

{{< include /dec/time/_watch.qmd >}}

The "Ticks" radio input above refers to the tick marks on the simulated watch face above and how many times the simulated watch ticks per [md](#md){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday"} ([&permil;](#permil){#permilliday .mono .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="per milliday"}). I used the [`librosa`](https://librosa.org) [Python](https://www.python.org) [library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Library_%28computing%29#:~:text=a%20collection%20of%20resources%20that%20can%20be%20used%20during%20software%20development) to determine that the [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo#:~:text=pace%20of%20a%20given%20composition) of the [1988]{.color88by100} song "[Don't Worry, Be Happy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don%27t_Worry,_Be_Happy#:~:text=a%201988%20song%20by%20Bobby%20McFerrin)" is [~]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="approximately"}100.566 [&permil;](#permil){.mono .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="per milliday"} or [~]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="approximately"}1.00566 per [cmd](#cmd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="centimillidays"} ([&thorn;](#per){#perbeat .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="perbeat"}). Whereas [&permil;](#permil){.mono .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="per milliday"} and [&thorn;](#per){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="perbeat"} measure [rates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rate_%28mathematics%29#:~:text=the%20denominator%20is%20a%20time%20duration), [md](#md){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday"} and [cmd](#cmd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="centimillidays"} measure
[durations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duration#:~:text=amount%20of%20time%20elapsed%20between%20two%20events).

Dec is not the first system to use [decimal time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal_time#France). During the [French Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Revolution), decimal time was mandatory for French public records for 197 days ([d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"}), from [1794]{.color94by100}+[205]{.color205by365} to [1795]{.color95by100}+[037]{.color037by365}. On [1998]{.color98by100}+[236]{.color236by365}, the Swatch corporation announced [Swatch Internet Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swatch_Internet_Time), which divides the day into 1000 ".beats" (a Swatch .beat is 1 [md](#md){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday"}, whereas a Dec beat is 1 [cmd](#cmd){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="centimilliday"}), only has one time zone, and is displayed by Dec as [mod](#mod){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="milliday of day"}&minus;[&beta;]{.color1by24}.

# Next {#next .unnumbered}

The next article in the [Dec section](/dec) of my [site](/) shows how we can combine [Dec dates](/dec/date) and times into [Dec snaps](/dec/snap)🫰, which are analogous to the [combined date and time representations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Combined_date_and_time_representations) in the [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#:~:text=an%20international%20standard%20covering%20the%20worldwide%20exchange%20and%20communication%20of%20date%20and%20time%2Drelated%20data) international standard for dates and times. The final article in the Dec section demonstrates how Dec dates, times, and snaps🫰can be paired up to express [time intervals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals:~:text=the%20intervening%20time%20between%20two%20time%20points) called Dec [spans](/dec/span)🌈.
